caption: The drawing displays two technical views of a table labeled "TIP TABLE" in black ink on a beige or light tan background. The left side of the image shows a front elevation view, with the tabletop depicted as a long horizontal rectangle measuring 45 1/2 inches across and 2 3/4 inches thick, featuring a scalloped detail along the lower edge of the apron beneath the top. The table is supported by a central, wide, turned pedestal base measuring 19 1/2 inches across at the bottom and 3/4 inch thick, with several decorative curves. The pedestal sits on a base that is rectangular in shape and 2 inches thick. The right side of the drawing presents a side elevation view, revealing the rectangular tabletop and apron, which has a scalloped edge at the bottom matching the front view. The apron is 4 1/2 inches high, and the space between the legs at the bottom is 17 inches. The legs, depicted as vertical rectangular shapes, are positioned at each end, with 4 1/2 inches of space from the ends of the tabletop. Several dimensions are marked with straight black lines and clear number notations. At the top right, the inscription reads "NEW YORK HISTORICAL SOCIETY, 170 CENTRAL PARK WEST." There are blue handwritten notations along the left margin, and the drawing uses only black lines and text on the neutral background, with no shading or coloring on the objects themselves.
title: Tip Table
